```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_ggplot2 <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

spice runs SPICE3 netlists on Dune, a circuit simulator derived from
Berkeley SPICE3f5, and hands the results back as tidy data. This
vignette runs one deck end to end: a second-order RLC low-pass driven
by a voltage step, with a transient and an AC analysis.

```{r setup}
library(spice)
```

## A deck

A deck is ordinary SPICE3 input. The first line is the title; the
analysis cards (`.tran`, `.ac`, ...) say what to compute. Here it is
given as text; `spice_run()` equally accepts the path of a `.cir` file.

```{r deck}
deck <- "RLC low-pass
vin in 0 pulse(0 1 0 1u) ac 1
r1 in mid 50
l1 mid out 1m
c1 out 0 1u
.tran 2u 1m
.ac dec 50 100 100k
.end"
```

## Running it

```{r run}
res <- spice_run(deck)
res
```

Each analysis produces a plot, named as SPICE3 names it in a rawfile.
Simulator options can be overridden from R, with the names and units of
the `.options` card:

```{r options}
tight <- spice_run(deck, options = list(reltol = 1e-5, method = "gear"))
```

## Tidy results

`spice_tidy()` (or `tibble::as_tibble()` of one plot) returns the long
format: one row per point and variable, with the plot's scale repeated
on every row. Its second argument picks plots, by label or by a short
name of the analysis (`"op"`, `"dc"`, `"tran"`, `"ac"`, ...).

```{r tidy}
tran <- spice_tidy(res, "tran")
tran
```

The third argument picks variables; a bare node name stands for its
voltage. The AC plot is complex, so instead of `value` it has `re` and
`im`, and with them `mag`, `db` and `phase` (in degrees).

```{r ac}
ac <- res |> spice_tidy("ac", "out")
ac[, c("scale", "db", "phase")]
```

`spice_wide()` is the other layout, for arithmetic between signals:
one row per point, the scale first and one column per variable.

```{r wide}
w <- res |> spice_wide("tran")
w
# The largest voltage across the inductor
max(abs(w$`v(mid)` - w$`v(out)`))
```

## Plotting the transient

```{r plot, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3.5}
library(ggplot2)
volts <- res |> spice_tidy("tran", c("in", "out"))
ggplot(volts, aes(scale * 1e3, value, colour = variable)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "time (ms)", y = "voltage (V)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Step response of the RLC low-pass")
```

For a quick look, `autoplot()` draws any plot with a scale:

```{r autoplot, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3.5}
autoplot(spice_plots(res)[["AC Analysis"]])
```

## Decks as chunks

Loading spice also gives knitr a `spice` engine. In R Markdown or
Quarto, a ```` ```{spice} ```` chunk holds a deck: the engine runs it,
prints the head of its tidy table, and leaves the result in a variable
named after the chunk label, ready for the R chunks below it (see
`?spice_knitr` for the chunk options).

````markdown
`r ''````{spice divider}
divider
v1 1 0 dc 0
r1 1 2 1k
r2 2 0 3k
.dc v1 0 10 1
.end
```
````

```{spice divider}
divider
v1 1 0 dc 0
r1 1 2 1k
r2 2 0 3k
.dc v1 0 10 1
.end
```

```{r divider-plot, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3}
autoplot(spice_plots(divider)[[1]])
```

## Circuits from figures

A schematic drawn in [pic](https://github.com/milkway/rpic-lang) with the
dune prelude (`resistor()`, `vsource()`, `npn()`, ...; the figure opts in
with `spice = 1`) is a deck too: `spice_pic()` extracts its netlist -- the
block labels are the refdes, the wires the nodes -- and `spice_run()` runs
the extraction. `spice_pic_svg()` draws the figure.

```{r pic}
fig <- ".PS
spice = 1
In: (0,1); Out: (2,1)
V1: vsource(In, (0,0), DC 5)
R1: resistor(In, Out, 1k)
R2: resistor(Out, (2,0), 3k)
line from R2.N to V1.N; ground(V1.N)
.op
.PE"
p <- spice_pic(fig)
cat(p$netlist)
spice_run(p) |> spice_op("out")
p$map$pins
```

## Exchanging rawfiles

Results write to and read from SPICE3 rawfiles, the format ngspice
reads and writes with `-r`:

```{r raw}
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".raw")
spice_write_raw(res, f)
back <- spice_read_raw(f)
identical(spice_tidy(back), spice_tidy(res))
```
